newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi stocks end sharply up on hopes of new leader.
newsitem.headline: Delhi stocks end sharply up on hopes of new leader.

text.p: Delhi stock prices ended sharply up in brisk trade on Friday as foreign and domestic financial institutions made sizeable purchases on hopes the United Front would elect a new leader, brokers said.
Traders said the closure of the country's other stock exchanges forced line operators to build edge positions on the local stock exchange which also aided the sentiment to improve.
The Delhi Stock Exchange Sensitive Index shot up 12.16 points or 1.5 percent to close at 782.04 points.

Shares of banking companies continued to hold the fancy of FIIs and domestic investors, enthused by a favourable half-yearly credit policy cutting bank interest rates by one percent to 11 percent, according to brokers.

"Apart from a flexible credit policy which is expected to ease the present tight money conditions, favourable developments on the political front also had a positive impact on market sentiment," said Yogesh Sethi of stockbrokers Vinayaka Investments.
"Expectations that the market leader Reliance Industries might come out with excellent working results also aided the upward trends," said another stock broker.
Reliance Industries Ltd, which led the trend-setter stocks, rose 5.10 rupees to 287 rupees following persistent buying by some FIIs and some short covering.
TISCO, another blue-chip stock, also attracted sizeable buying from FIIs and domestic investors and ended 7.80 rupees higher at 177.30 rupees while TELCO moved 4.60 rupees to 389.10 rupees.

Shares of State Bank of India, the country's largest commercial banking firm, traded heavily throughout the session as FIIs and speculators took positions in the wake of the RBI's new credit policy, and shot up 6.90 rupees to 304.15 rupees.
Shares of ACC flared up 38 rupees to 1433, largely driven by Bombay-based operators, followed by short covering.
ITC Ltd ended 6.50 rupees higher at 424 rupees on massive buying by FIIs, coupled with huge short covering.
Stocks of Oriental Bank of Commerce gained 3.05 rupees to close at 78.75 rupees on FII buying.
BSES Ltd rose 2.50 rupees to 221.50 rupees, Larsen and Toubro rose 4.50 rupees to 225, Hindustan Lever 10 to 1050, and IPCL 2.10 to 146 rupees.
